name: Deep Teal
lede: Deep Teal is a darker, bluer-green reading of [[teal]], named for the duck's head after which teal itself is named, and filed in the 1955 ISCC-NBS system and the 2010 xkcd color survey.

sections.title: A modifier on a bird's name
sections.body:
The name follows the library's modifier grammar, *deep* plus [[teal]]; teal itself is named for the dark green patch on a teal duck's head, a connection the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 inherited when it filed this chip into block 164, named moderate bluish green in that system's own list [1]. The xkcd online color survey of 2010 independently settled on the same name for roughly the same hex, from crowd-sourced labels rather than any dictionary [1].

Its nearest look-alike on file is [[dark-teal]], about 3.2 units off, with [[kremlin]] close behind and one named child variant, [[deep-teal-green]], branching from it [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This match appears in 0.23% of the 23,781 paintings in our archive (54 paintings, as photographed); the within-painting lens narrows that to 27 [3]. In our archive it is rarer than 58% of the named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, present in 0.5% of the 1,674 paintings we have from that decade (8 paintings), 3.4 times the rate its museums would predict [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color, in 63% of its 27 appearances by lightness rank within the painting [3]. The earliest match dates to 1430, 525 years before the name's 1955 record, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin and a look-alike hue in an aged photograph is not proof of a pigment or dye [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so the match is a screen comparison, not a pigment identification [3].
